---
name: work-planner
description: >-
  Plans and maintains agent-engineering work on GitHub: proposals, initiatives, epics, tasks and theme boards. Use to propose work or scope a problem; plan or break down work; raise, restructure, align or renumber an initiative or epic; check issue format, criteria, dependencies or delivery; fold review findings into issues; sync completed work and close what is finished; advance a board, decide what moves to ready or what to pick up next; deliver board work or dispatch ready tasks; understand or explain a pull request, write its architecture overview or diagram its changes; hoist, triage or find a home for orphan issues; produce a standup or Slack status update; or revise the work-planner skill itself.
---

# Work Planner

Work Planner plans work as GitHub issues and keeps the plan current until the work is delivered. The issues are the plan:

- **Proposal**  States the problem and the goal, with no Work Breakdown.
- **Initiative**  States a goal and lists its epics.
- **Epic**  Lists its tasks in a Work Breakdown table.
- **Task**  One pull request's worth of work.
- **Standalone issue**  Work outside any initiative.
- **[Hot-fix](artifacts/hotfix-body.md)**  A fix to a long-lived branch beside all queued work.

Each theme's project board shows where its items stand. The [proposals board](configuration.md#proposals-board) holds proposals. A planning record holds what an initiative leaves out: the evidence, the decisions and each review.

Read [Rules](rules.md) and [Conventions](conventions.md) before selecting a mode.

## Modes

Select the mode as appropriate to fulfill the user request:

- **[Propose](modes/propose-mode.md)**
  - Forward-looking, scoped to one problem
  - Scoping a problem nothing is planned against yet
  - Raising a proposal issue with optional board placement
- **[Plan](modes/plan-mode.md)**
  - Forward-looking, scoped to one approved proposal
  - Turning an approved proposal into initiatives
  - Raising, breaking down and restructuring initiatives and epics
  - Review passes of a plan against its goal, dependencies included
  - Renumbering of epics and tasks
  - Folding review findings into issues
- **[Align](modes/align-mode.md)**
  - Backward-looking, scoped to one epic, initiative or board
  - Checks of existing issues against their templates and the rules that bind them, with fixes
  - Acceptance criteria checked for verifiability and against the sources the initiative marks
  - Epic branch structure and task pull request bases brought to the delivery shape
- **[Sync](modes/sync-mode.md)**
  - Backward-looking, scoped to one epic, initiative or board
  - Delivery recorded against the issues that planned it
  - Closure of complete task issues, epics and initiatives
  - The theme board brought current with its issues
- **[Advance](modes/advance-mode.md)**
  - Forward-looking, scoped to one board
  - Placement of initiatives and epics as In Progress or as Ready, and of hot-fixes as their [Board Status](artifacts/hotfix.md#board-status) gives
  - A parallel work map for initiatives with no priority
- **[Deliver](modes/deliver-mode.md)**
  - Forward-looking, scoped to one board
  - Delivery of a theme board's work, each unit planned, implemented and raised as a pull request
  - Dispatch of one session per unit of work
  - Merging task pull requests through the shared delivery procedure
- **[Understand](modes/understand-mode.md)**
  - Backward-looking, scoped to one pull request
  - An architecture overview of one pull request
  - Structural and functional diagrams of its changes
  - The order to read the diff in
- **[Hoist](modes/hoist-mode.md)**
  - Forward-looking, scoped to a repository's orphan issues
  - Discovery of orphan issues
  - Placements for each in an existing or new initiative, epic or task, or as a hot-fix
- **[Standup](modes/standup-mode.md)**
  - Backward-looking, scoped to one board's reporting window
  - Standup summaries of a theme's board for a Slack channel
- **[Revise](modes/revise-mode.md)**
  - Forward-looking, scoped to this skill's own files
  - Changes to SKILL.md, its modes, artifacts, references and scripts

## Dependencies

- **GitHub CLI (`gh`).**
- **Sandbox.** (`scripts/sbx`).
- **Python 3.10 or later.**
- **git.**
- **GitNexus.**
- **Sub-agents.**
- **Epic-base merge permission.**
  The agent harness grants the [Merge Permission](artifacts/pull-request.md#merge-permission) Deliver needs.

# Rules

- **Linked sections.**
  Read a heading-linked section and its subsections, stopping before the next heading of equal or higher level. Read that file's Prerequisites first; reading prerequisites does not execute procedures. A mode named in another mode's Prerequisites is read as a document, and its own Prerequisites load only where a step runs it. Preserve boundaries in batched reads and recover truncated output. Reuse complete prerequisites already read at the same revision. Explicit whole-document requirements still apply.
- **Decisions.**
  Ask one at a time, following the [interview rules](guidelines.md#modes). A decision the run's [allowance](artifacts/plan-change.md#allowance) covers is taken with its recommended option rather than asked. Record each decision in the affected issues and, when there is one, the planning record.
- **Layers.**
  Modes, protocols, artifacts. A mode aggregates protocol calls, as an application calls services; a protocol runs artifact operations and other protocols; an artifact runs neither. A call goes down the stack, never up. A mode reaches an artifact operation directly only where no protocol owns that change.
- **Execution.**
  A call passes its named inputs. A protocol is one change that lands in several artifacts together, and is run whole. Run another mode, a protocol, or a named subsection only where the procedure calls it; finish that call and return its result before continuing, unless the procedure explicitly dispatches concurrent work.

# Conventions

- **Session.**
  Once per session, before the first `gh` call, unset `GH_TOKEN` and `GITHUB_TOKEN` so `gh` uses its keyring login. Where shell state does not persist between commands, confirm instead that neither is set in the shell profile.
- **Repository.**
  `gh` resolves `{owner}/{repo}` from the git remote of the directory it runs in, so run `gh` commands inside a checkout of the repository that holds the issues. `{other}` is a further repository the board's issues live in.
- **Checkouts.**
  A command that runs git or GitNexus where it stands declares `**Acts on:** the checkout it runs in.`, and each call to it, or to an operation running it, names one as `the <name> checkout`. Each mode and protocol declares `**Runs in:** the <name> checkout.`, as does a procedure subsection running elsewhere.
  - `project`  The repository's main working tree.
  - `epic base`  An epic base's worktree.
  - `unit`  A unit's task worktree.
  - `engineering`  The [engineering branch](configuration.md#planning-records)'s worktree.
  - `review`  A pull request's detached review worktree.
- **Bodies.**
  - Bodies and long comments always go through a file (`-F body=@file`), never inline, which avoids quoting.
  - **Example.**  workflow-server's dynamic-shell restrictions deny a body inlined in the command.
  - A plan's draft bodies are files of its [planning record](artifacts/planning-record.md#layout). Keep every other body file in a working directory outside the repository.
- **Scripts.**
  Scripts run under `sbx`, invoked by its absolute path from `<workspace>`, the checkout holding this skill. A script that reaches the tracker calls `gh` itself, and one that adds a worktree writes the repository's git directory, which `sbx` leaves read-only; each runs from `<workspace>` outside `sbx`.
- **Boards.**
  A project board sits under `users/{owner}`, or `orgs/{owner}` when `gh api repos/{owner}/{repo} --jq .owner.type` is `Organization`.
- **Example values.**  Substitute the real ones:
  - `936` an initiative issue, `943` and `937` its epics, `637` a task issue, `874` an orphan, `946` an initiative off the board, `960` a proposal;
  - `950` a pull request, `I07` and `I08` initiative numbers;
  - board `9`, workflow-server's Canon theme, and `419167630` its Status field id;
  - `1` the Initiative Template board, `13` a board copied from it;
  - `14` the Proposals Template, `15` the Proposals board;
  - `m2ux` the user.
  - `<checkout>` any checkout of the project, a linked worktree included.

# Configuration

The deployed board values, planning-record location and reporting default.

## Boards

### Theme Boards

The copy source is the open board titled `Initiative Template`. Its `Status` field carries Backlog, Ready, In Progress, In Review and Done.

### Proposals Board

The board is titled `Proposals`. Its copy source is the open board titled `Proposals Template`. That template carries Priority: High, Medium and Low, and its view is a board grouped by Status.

## Themes

**Example.** workflow-server's themes.

| Theme | Label | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Canon | `theme:canon` | Definitions Checked Against the Design Canon |
| Language | `theme:language` | The Definition Language and Its Rules |
| Mechanical | `theme:mechanical` | The Engine That Runs Definitions |
| Delivery | `theme:delivery` | What Reaches Agents and Hosts |
| Planning | `theme:planning` | [Project 17 — Process: How Work Is Planned and Delivered](https://github.com/users/m2ux/projects/17) |

## Planning Records

Planning records live under `artifacts/planning/` on the `engineering` branch.

## Standup

The default window opens a week before today.

# Plan Mode

Scopes the solution: the design, the criteria, and the breakdown of an initiative and its epics, and keeps them current as work lands.

**Runs in:** the project checkout.

## Prerequisites

Read these files first.

- [Lane](../artifacts/lane.md)
- [Propose Mode](propose-mode.md)
- [Guidelines](../guidelines.md)
- [Planning Record](../artifacts/planning-record.md)
- [Pull Request](../artifacts/pull-request.md)
- [Issue](../artifacts/issue.md)
- [Initiative Issue Body](../artifacts/initiative-issue-body.md)
- [Epic Issue Body](../artifacts/epic-issue-body.md)
- [Work Item](../artifacts/work-item.md)
- [Repository Labels](../artifacts/repository-labels.md)
- [Issue Body](../artifacts/issue-body.md)
- [Epic](../artifacts/epic.md)
- [Delivery Branches](../artifacts/delivery-branches.md)
- [Sync Mode](sync-mode.md)
- [Review Finding](../artifacts/review-finding.md)
- [Goal Trace](../artifacts/goal-trace.md)
- [Dependency Graph](../artifacts/dependency-graph.md)

## Procedure

The main path meets [Outcomes](#outcomes).

1. **Take the proposal.**
   - When the user names a proposal, its associated issue body defines the problem scope.
   - When the user names an initiative that already exists, fetch its body with [Read Tracker Issue](../artifacts/issue.md#read-tracker-issue). That body defines the problem scope, and no proposal is raised for work it already carries.
   - When neither a proposal nor an existing initiative is named:
     - Run [Propose Mode](propose-mode.md) with the user's goal.
     - Resume this selection step with its published proposal; an unresolved proposal blocks initiative drafting.
2. **Prepare the planning record.**
   - For an initiative, epic or complex plan, call [Populate Planning Record](../artifacts/planning-record.md#populate-planning-record) with the record identity, folder and supplied evidence files.
   - Use [Layout](../artifacts/planning-record.md#layout) for draft paths.
   - Run [Publish Planning Record](../artifacts/planning-record.md#publish-planning-record) for the record's folder.
3. **Draft each initiative body.**
   - For a new initiative, obtain its proposed prefix through [Select Tracker Number](../artifacts/issue.md#select-tracker-number) with the initiative prefix letter.
   - Run [Draft Initiative Issue Body](../artifacts/initiative-issue-body.md#draft-initiative-issue-body) for each initiative with the scoped proposal, confirmed goal clauses, requirement sources, epic summaries and an output path in the record's folder. The epics' acceptance criteria carry the detail that makes the initiative's criteria true.
4. **Populate the epics.**
   - Ask once per initiative whether it uses lanes as an [Interview](../guidelines.md#modes), recommending a choice from its proposed parallel delivery. Reuse the initiative's recorded decision when it has one.
   - For an initiative using lanes, propose each task row's [Lane](../artifacts/lane.md#index) index as a map for the user to confirm, assigning joined rows together as [Unit Consistency](../artifacts/lane.md#unit-consistency) requires. Record the confirmed map in the planning record. For an initiative without lanes, leave the row lanes empty.
   - Run [Populate Epic Issue Body](../artifacts/epic-issue-body.md#populate-epic-issue-body) for each epic and each new task row, passing each confirmed optional lane index with the row and an output path in the record's folder.
   - Call [Populate Work Item](../artifacts/work-item.md#populate-work-item) for each task with its scope, design, the component its implementation extends, criteria, test requirements and an output file in the record's folder.
   - Register each draft body and returned work-item file in the planning record.
   - Resolve Open Questions before work starts.
   - Run [Check Dependencies and Numbering](../artifacts/dependency-graph.md#check-dependencies-and-numbering) across the drafts and the returned work-item files.
   - Return each epic draft and its format results to the review step.
5. **Review the drafts.**
   Follow [Review Initiative Goal](../artifacts/goal-trace.md#review-initiative-goal).
   - Run [Report Review Finding](../artifacts/review-finding.md#report-review-finding) for each returned finding, with its scope, evidence and proposed resolution.
   - Apply each confirmed resolution to the drafts:
     - For a local epic finding, call Populate Epic Issue Body with the confirmed Proposal, row and criterion changes, including every new or renumbered criterion in Coverage.
     - For a confirmed distinct concern:
       - Draft its own epic and initiative row.
       - Repeat ordering review for the new epic and initiative row.
   - Record the finding, resolution and decision in the planning record.
   - Repeat Review Initiative Goal with the revised initiative and epic bodies and retained goal clauses and sources. No issue is created while a content or structural finding remains. Unresolved links to unpublished issues are recorded with their intended row identities and resolved during publication; no other finding is deferred.
   - An acceptance criterion is created only once it meets [Initiative Acceptance Criteria](../artifacts/initiative-issue-body.md#initiative-acceptance-criteria).
6. **Publish.**
   Put the proposed [Epic Priority](../artifacts/dependency-graph.md#epic-priority) map for the reviewed epics to the user as an [Interview](../guidelines.md#modes), the proposal the recommended answer.
   - Take the positive integer the user confirms for each epic.
   - Call [Ensure Repository Labels](../artifacts/repository-labels.md#ensure-repository-labels) with the required definitions, the priority label each confirmed number names among them, before saving the issues.
   - For a new initiative:
     - Call [Select Tracker Number](../artifacts/issue.md#select-tracker-number) with the initiative prefix letter.
     - Save it through [Save Tracker Issue](../artifacts/issue.md#save-tracker-issue), using temporary epic-row links until issue identities exist.
     - Save the epics in dependency order, each carrying its confirmed priority label.
     - Replace every temporary link in the initiative and epic bodies with the saved issue identity.
     - Confirm no unresolved epic placeholder remains.
   - Call [Validate Epic Body](../artifacts/epic-issue-body.md#validate-epic-body) with the saved initiative context.
   - Call [Validate Initiative Body](../artifacts/initiative-issue-body.md#validate-initiative-body) with every saved epic.
   - Resolve findings.
   - Save the corrected bodies.
   - Update the planning record with evidence, decisions and issue links.
   - Run Publish Planning Record for the record's folder.
7. **Keep the goal current.**
   When the goal, a criterion, a Problem, a Proposal or an epic changes:
   - Repeat Review Initiative Goal with the revised bodies and current sources.
   - Run Report Review Finding for each finding.
   - Apply confirmed resolutions.
   - Repeat that review until clear.
   - After each round, run [Check Round of Edits](../artifacts/issue-body.md#check-round-of-edits) on affected bodies.
   - Whenever tasks, edges or a work item's component change, repeat Check Dependencies and Numbering.
     - Put the proposed Epic Priority map to the user again where the edges or the contention moved an epic's number.
     - Save each confirmed change as that epic's priority label.
   - Save affected bodies through Save Tracker Issue, matching titles to current numbers and Coverage to current criteria.
   - Keep the record's body files as the source for the next pass.
   - Update work-item files and the README inventory for added, renamed or removed tasks.
   - Update the planning record.
   - Run Publish Planning Record for the record's folder.
8. **Prepare epic delivery.**
   Before any task starts:
   - Resolve every Open Question with the user.
   - Record the answer.
   - Update the affected bodies, removing each settled question.
   - Split multi-condition criteria at the end of the list.
   - Update Coverage for the split criteria.
   - Run [Check Epic Prerequisites](../artifacts/epic.md#check-epic-prerequisites) with current initiative and prerequisite evidence; stop on a failed or incomplete result.
   - After prerequisites pass, call [Prepare Delivery Bases](../artifacts/delivery-branches.md#prepare-delivery-bases) with the project checkout.
   - Run [Publish Pull Request](../artifacts/pull-request.md#publish-pull-request) to retarget each affected open task pull request to its epic base.
   - Repeat goal and ordering review on changed bodies before returning readiness.
9. **Record delivered work.**
   When work has landed:
   - Run [Sync Mode](sync-mode.md) for the affected initiative.
   - For an unplaced task issue:
     - Add its row through Populate Epic Issue Body.
     - Save that body.
     - Repeat Sync Mode with the refreshed epic.
   - Return the saved delivery state or blockers.

## Outcomes

- **A scoped initiative.**
  The user has an initiative scoped to the proposal they named, or to a proposal raised for that problem.
- **Several initiatives.**
  One proposal may become several initiatives. A partition by solution maturity, such as an MVP demo, a functional prototype, and a production-intent version, is an example of that result. Those initiatives may run in series or in parallel. The example does not limit the partition.
- **A goal made true.**
  Each clause of the goal the user confirmed is made true by the initiative's criteria, and the epics the initiative lists are the work that delivers those criteria.
- **Epics that start together.**
  The user has settled which of the initiative's epics start alongside each other, from a proposal the dependency graph makes.
- **Review before creation.**
  Findings on that initiative are folded in before any of its issues are created.

# Propose Mode

Scopes one problem: the friction, the evidence, and the boundary, and states the goal as clauses the user confirms. It raises one proposal on the proposals board.

**Runs in:** the project checkout.

## Prerequisites

Read these files first.

- [Proposal Body](../artifacts/proposal-body.md)
- [Repository Labels](../artifacts/repository-labels.md)
- [Issue](../artifacts/issue.md)
- [Board](../artifacts/board.md)

## Procedure

The main path meets [Outcomes](#outcomes).

1. **Understand the problem.**
   Ask the user until the friction and the boundary are clear.
   - State the goal back as clauses meeting [Goal](../artifacts/proposal-body.md#goal).
   - Have the user confirm those clauses.
2. **Gather evidence.**
   - Measure the current state: counts, paths, and file:line.
   - Delegate broad sweeps to parallel sub-agents.
   - Spot-check what they return before recording it.
3. **Draft the body.**
   Run [Populate Proposal Body](../artifacts/proposal-body.md#populate-proposal-body) with the confirmed problem, evidence, goal clauses, boundary and output body path. The local file is the source for the issue.
   - Obtain the proposal's number through [Select Tracker Number](../artifacts/issue.md#select-tracker-number) with the proposal prefix letter, and carry it in the title.
   - The goal clauses are the clauses the user confirmed. The Non-Goals are the boundary.
   - The design, the acceptance criteria, and the breakdown belong to a later goal.
4. **Validate.**
   Call [Validate Proposal Body](../artifacts/proposal-body.md#validate-proposal-body) with the draft issue JSON and output file.
   - Resolve each finding.
   - Update the draft.
   - Repeat Validate Proposal Body with the revised JSON and the same output path. Proceed to publication only when validation passes.
5. **Publish.**
   Call [Ensure Repository Labels](../artifacts/repository-labels.md#ensure-repository-labels) with the proposal's required label definitions.
   - Pass the validated body, title and labels to [Save Tracker Issue](../artifacts/issue.md#save-tracker-issue), leaving it unassigned.
6. **Confirm placement.**
   Ask whether to add the issue to the proposals board.
   - On acceptance, continue to the place step.
   - On a decline, skip placement and continue to the report step with the issue URL.
   - Wait for an unanswered decision.
7. **Place.**
   Call [Locate Project Board](../artifacts/board.md#locate-project-board) for proposals.
   - Create an absent board through [Create Proposals Board](../artifacts/board.md#create-proposals-board).
   - Read the saved issue id through [Read Tracker Issue](../artifacts/issue.md#read-tracker-issue).
   - Run [Place Issue on Board](../artifacts/board.md#place-issue-on-board) with that id and initial status Suggested.
   - Leave the issue unassigned.
8. **Report.**
   Give the issue's URL, and the board's when the issue was placed.

## Outcomes

- **A scoped problem.**
  The user has one problem scoped, and has confirmed its goal.
- **One proposal.**
  The user has that problem raised as one proposal.
- **On the proposals board.**
  When the user wants the proposal on the proposals board, it is there, raised, and unassigned.

# Board

The theme or proposals board, its membership and each item's status.

## Prerequisites

Read these files first.

- For proposals-board selection or creation, read [Proposals Board Configuration](../configuration.md#proposals-board).
- For theme-board creation, read [Theme Board Configuration](../configuration.md#theme-boards).

## Operations

### *Select* Project Board

The theme or proposals board the request names.

**Inputs:** Board owner and either a theme name or the proposals-board selection.

1. Run [Find Theme Board](#find-theme-board) for the named theme, or [Find Proposals Board](#find-proposals-board) when the request names proposals. The selection meets [Themes](#themes) or [Proposals](#proposals).
2. Return a missing-selection result when neither a theme nor proposals is specified; the caller obtains that choice.
3. Return the selected board number, or an absent-board result for [Copy Project Board](#copy-project-board). Work one board at a time.

### *Copy* Project Board

A missing theme board, or a missing proposals board.

**Inputs:** Board owner, repository, selected board kind, theme title and originating proposal record when applicable.

1. When no open board has the [proposals title](../configuration.md#proposals-board), run [Create Proposals Board](#create-proposals-board). The copy source and the title meet [Proposals](#proposals).
2. When the selected theme board is absent:
   - Run [Create Theme Board](#create-theme-board) with the owner, repository, theme title and originating proposal record when applicable.
   - Require the new theme's label and board before an initiative takes that theme.

### *Create* Proposals Board

A new proposals board linked to the supplied repository.

**Inputs:** Board owner and repository.

1. Run [Find Board Template](#find-board-template) with the owner and the exact [proposals-template title](../configuration.md#proposals-board).
2. Use the returned number as the copy source.
3. Run [Copy Board Template](#copy-board-template) with that template number, the owner and the [proposals title](../configuration.md#proposals-board).
4. Retain the new board number. The copy meets [Proposals](#proposals).
5. Run [Link Board to Repository](#link-board-to-repository) with the owner, new board number and repository.
6. Return the new board number after linking succeeds.

### *Create* Theme Board

A new theme board linked to the supplied repository.

**Inputs:** Board owner, repository, theme title and originating proposal record when applicable.

1. Require the originating proposal record for a proposal-derived board; return a missing-input finding when its designator is unavailable.
2. Run [Find Board Template](#find-board-template) with the owner and the exact [theme-template title](../configuration.md#theme-boards).
3. Use the returned number as the copy source.
4. Run [Copy Board Template](#copy-board-template) with that template number, the owner and the title required by [One Board Per Theme](#one-board-per-theme).
5. Retain the new board number. The copy carries the [theme-board fields](../configuration.md#theme-boards).
6. Run [Link Board to Repository](#link-board-to-repository) with the owner, new board number and repository.
7. Return the new board number after linking succeeds.

### *Place* Issue on Board

One issue's membership and initial status.

**Inputs:** Board owner and number, issue id and selected initial status.

1. Run [Fetch Board Fields](#fetch-board-fields) for the Status options, using the caller's supplied board and issue identities.
2. Run [Add Issue to Board](#add-issue-to-board) with the issue id.
3. Run [Set Item Status](#set-item-status) with the caller's selected status and the matching field and option ids.
4. Run [Fetch Board Item](#fetch-board-item) for the saved item.

### *Read* Board State

The selected board's items and status fields.

**Inputs:** Existing board owner and number, as [Select Project Board](#select-project-board) or [Copy Project Board](#copy-project-board) returns them, whether the caller ran that operation or carries its result.

1. Run [Find Status Field](#find-status-field) for the board number.
2. Run [Fetch Board Items with Status](#fetch-board-items-with-status), passing that field id and board number.
3. Return the items, Status field, item ids and the board's [Repositories](#repositories) to the caller.

### *Read* Board Assignee

The authenticated login available for board assignments.

**Inputs:** Authenticated repository access.

1. Run [Find User](#find-user).
2. Return its login for the caller's assignment decisions.

### *Read* Board Configuration

One board's field definitions and requested item state.

**Inputs:** Board owner and number, output paths and optional item identity.

1. Run [Fetch Board Fields](#fetch-board-fields) for the supplied board.
2. When a single item is requested for write confirmation, run [Fetch Board Item](#fetch-board-item). A list snapshot may lag a write.
3. Return the field definitions and requested current item.

### *Locate* Project Board

The board identity matching a supplied purpose or theme.

**Inputs:** Owner and proposals-board purpose or theme title.

1. Run [Find Proposals Board](#find-proposals-board) for proposals, or [Find Theme Board](#find-theme-board) for a theme.
2. Return the identity or an absent-board finding for the caller's selection or creation path.

## Fields

### Themes

Every initiative belongs to one theme, and each theme has one project board. Each project names its own themes.

Project examples are in [Themes](../configuration.md#themes).

### One Theme

An initiative carries one `theme:*` label, and each of its epics carries the same one.

### One Board Per Theme

- A proposal-derived board title is the originating proposal's exact `[Pxx]` designator, a space, the theme name, a colon, and its description: `[P03] Canon: Definitions Checked Against the Design Canon`. Preserve the proposal's digits exactly. A board with no originating proposal uses `Name: Description`.
- It is linked to the repository.
- It holds the theme's initiatives, their epics and their task issues, and its hot-fixes.

### Repositories

A board's repositories are those its items' issues live in, read from each item's issue, deduplicated and ordered with the board's own repository first. An item whose issue is unreadable leaves the list incomplete, which is reported rather than filled by assumption.

### Assignees

An issue at Ready, In Progress, In Review or Done is assigned to the user; one in Backlog has no assignee. An assignee is set on the issue, not on the board item, so the call that changes one acts on the issue.

### Standalone Issues

A standalone issue sits on no board.

### Proposals

- The [configured board](../configuration.md#proposals-board) holds proposal issues, the incoming funnel for work that may become an initiative.
- **Suggested.**
  Raised, and nobody has taken it up. A new proposal lands here, with no assignee.
- **Considering.**
  Someone is weighing the goal, the evidence and the criteria. That person is the assignee.
- **Approved.**
  Qualified to become an initiative. The assignee is the user.
- **Held.**
  Not now. It stays on the board, with no assignee.
- **Declined.**
  It will not become an initiative. It has no assignee.

## Commands

### Find Board Template

Prints the number of the open board with the supplied exact template title.

**Inputs:** Board owner and template title.

```bash
gh api --paginate "users/<owner>/projectsV2?per_page=100" --jq '.[] | select(.closed | not) | select(.title == "<template-title>") | .number'
```

### Copy Board Template

Copies the supplied template into a new open board with the supplied title and prints its number.

**Inputs:** Board owner, template board number and new board title.

- The copy's JSON is one project; `.number` identifies the new board.

```bash
gh project copy '<template-number>' --source-owner '<owner>' --target-owner '<owner>' --title '<board-title>' --format json --jq .number
```

### Link Board to Repository

Links one board to the supplied repository.

**Inputs:** Board owner, board number and repository.

```bash
gh project link '<board-number>' --owner '<owner>' --repo '<repo>'
```

### Find Proposals Board

Prints the number of the open [proposals board](../configuration.md#proposals-board).

**Inputs:** Board owner.

```bash
gh api --paginate "users/<owner>/projectsV2?per_page=100" --jq '.[] | select(.closed | not) | select(.title == "Proposals") | .number'
```

### Add Issue to Board

Adds the caller-supplied issue id to a board and prints the new item's id. The input is the issue id, not its number.

**Inputs:** Board owner and number, and issue id.

```bash
gh api --method POST 'users/<owner>/projectsV2/<board-number>/items' -f type=Issue -F 'id=<issue-id>' --jq .id
```

**Example:**

```bash
gh api --method POST 'users/<owner>/projectsV2/13/items' -f type=Issue -F id=3040123456 --jq .id
```

### Set Item Status

Sets one board item's Status.

**Inputs:** Board owner and number, item id, and input file containing the Status field id and selected option id.

The input body names the Status field id and option id from [Fetch Board Fields](#fetch-board-fields): `{"fields":[{"id":<status-field-id>,"value":"<status-option-id>"}]}`. Substitute the field id as a JSON integer and the option id as a JSON string.

**Example payload:** `{"fields":[{"id":419167630,"value":"OPTION"}]}`.

```bash
gh api --method PATCH 'users/<owner>/projectsV2/<board-number>/items/<item-id>' --input '<status-input-file>' --jq .id
```

**Example:**

```bash
gh api --method PATCH 'users/<owner>/projectsV2/13/items/1001' --input status-backlog.json --jq .id
```

### Remove Board Item

Removes one item from a board, leaving its issue as it stands.

**Inputs:** Board owner and number, and the item id [Read Board State](#read-board-state) returns.

```bash
gh api --method DELETE 'users/<owner>/projectsV2/<board-number>/items/<item-id>'
```

**Example:**

```bash
gh api --method DELETE 'users/<owner>/projectsV2/9/items/1001'
```

### Fetch Board Fields

Saves a board's fields.

**Inputs:** Board owner, board number and destination file.

```bash
gh api --paginate "users/<owner>/projectsV2/<board-number>/fields?per_page=100" > '<board-fields-file>'
```

**Example:**

```bash
gh api --paginate "users/<owner>/projectsV2/9/fields?per_page=100" > fields.json
```

### Find Theme Board

Prints the number of the open board for one theme, by its theme name after any proposal designator.

**Inputs:** Board owner and theme name.

```bash
gh api --paginate "users/<owner>/projectsV2?per_page=100" --jq '.[] | select(.closed | not) | select(.title | sub("^\\[P[0-9]+\\] "; "") | startswith("<theme-name>: ")) | .number'
```

**Example:**

```bash
gh api --paginate "users/<owner>/projectsV2?per_page=100" --jq '.[] | select(.closed | not) | select(.title | sub("^\\[P[0-9]+\\] "; "") | startswith("Canon: ")) | .number'
```

### Find Status Field

Prints the id of a board's Status field.

**Inputs:** Board owner and number.

```bash
gh api --paginate "users/<owner>/projectsV2/<board-number>/fields?per_page=100" --jq '.[] | select(.name == "Status") | .id'
```

**Example:**

```bash
gh api --paginate "users/<owner>/projectsV2/9/fields?per_page=100" --jq '.[] | select(.name == "Status") | .id'
```

### Fetch Board Items with Status

Saves a board's items with their Status, each carrying its issue whole.

**Inputs:** Board owner and number, Status field id and destination file.

```bash
gh api --paginate "users/<owner>/projectsV2/<board-number>/items?per_page=100&fields=<status-field-id>" > '<board-items-file>'
```

**Example:**

```bash
gh api --paginate "users/<owner>/projectsV2/9/items?per_page=100&fields=419167630" > items.json
```

### Fetch Board Item

Reads one board item, including its current Status.

**Inputs:** Board owner and number, item id and Status field id.

```bash
gh api "users/<owner>/projectsV2/<board-number>/items/<item-id>?fields=<status-field-id>"
```

**Example:**

```bash
gh api "users/<owner>/projectsV2/9/items/1001?fields=419167630"
```

### Find User

Prints the login `gh` runs as, the user assigned to work from Ready on.

**Inputs:** Authenticated repository access.

```bash
gh api user --jq .login
```

# Repository Labels

The labels available for issue metadata in one repository.

## Operations

### *Ensure* Repository Labels

The required label definitions available for issue publication.

**Inputs:** Repository and required label names, colours and descriptions.

1. Run [List Labels](#list-labels) for the repository.
2. Compare the returned labels with the supplied required names.
3. Run [Create Label](#create-label) for each absent required definition.
4. Return the available labels; an unknown definition is a finding for the caller to resolve before publication.

## Fields

### Label Identity

Each label has a name, colour and description. Issue assignments use labels that exist in the repository.

## Commands

### List Labels

Lists the labels that exist in the repository.

**Inputs:** Repository.

```bash
gh api "repos/<owner>/<repo>/labels?per_page=100" --jq '.[].name'
```

### Create Label

Creates the label specified by its name, colour and description.

**Inputs:** Repository, label name, colour and description.

```bash
gh api --method POST 'repos/<owner>/<repo>/labels' -f name='<label>' -f color='<hex-colour>' -f description='<description>' --jq .name
```

reads.requested_text:
## Procedure

The main path meets [Outcomes](#outcomes).

1. **Select.**
   Select an initiative with its open epics, or the epics the user names.
   - Run [Read Tracker Issue](../artifacts/issue.md#read-tracker-issue) for each selected issue before inspecting its Open Questions or format.
   - Use the returned current JSON and body in the following checks.
   - For an epic with Open Questions:
     - Obtain the user's decision on each question.
     - Apply confirmed resolutions through [Apply Body Corrections](../artifacts/issue-body.md#apply-body-corrections) with the epic template and field conditions.
     - Publish through [Save Tracker Issue](../artifacts/issue.md#save-tracker-issue).
     - Fetch the saved epic.
     - Continue only when its Open Questions section is resolved; otherwise return the unresolved questions as blockers.
   - For an issue rejected by [Validate Issue Body](../artifacts/issue-body.md#validate-issue-body):
     - Run [Repair Issue Format](../artifacts/issue-body.md#repair-issue-format) with that issue identity, current JSON, kind template and field conditions, required related evidence and output body path.
     - When it returns, fetch the saved body again.
     - Validate that saved body before continuing to the fetch step.
     - Return a remaining format failure as a blocker.
2. **Fetch.**
   - Run [Read Tracker Issue](../artifacts/issue.md#read-tracker-issue) for each issue, including each task issue under an epic being synced, titled as [Titles](../artifacts/task-body.md#titles) states.
   - Run [Read Delivery Evidence](../artifacts/delivery-evidence.md#read-delivery-evidence) with the selected repositories and initiative prefix, the fetched initiative, epic and task issue JSON, authenticated access and destination snapshot files.
   - Use its returned pull request records, complete issue-link snapshot and findings in the following steps.
   - Run [Confirm Repository Auto-Close](../artifacts/issue.md#confirm-repository-auto-close) for the repository holding the issues, which gates every link, merge and closure this run makes.
   - Capture each issue's Development links.
3. **Unnamed deliveries.**
   When the user says work has landed but no pull request names its epic:
   - Find the pull request.
   - Confirm it with the user.
   - Give it the epic's reference, `[I07:E00] Purpose`, with [Publish Pull Request](../artifacts/pull-request.md#publish-pull-request).
   - Run [Read Initiative Pull Requests](../artifacts/pull-request.md#read-initiative-pull-requests) again, with the fetched issue files.
   - Run [Fetch Pull Request Issue Links](../artifacts/pull-request.md#fetch-pull-request-issue-links) again.
4. **Match pull requests to tasks.**
   Run [Inspect Epic Delivery](../artifacts/epic.md#inspect-epic-delivery) for each epic.
   - Use the unmatched and in-flight results defined in [Delivery Findings](../artifacts/epic.md#delivery-findings).
   - Read its changes and description against the tasks' Descriptions.
   - Name the tasks it works on: one task, or tasks that name each other in Joins.
   - Put any match that is not clear to the user.
5. **Sync each task issue.**
   For a task with a delivering pull request, open or merged, run [Verify Selected Criteria](../artifacts/acceptance-criteria.md#verify-selected-criteria) with its current body, selected criteria, delivery evidence, revisions, named instruments and the project checkout.
   - Run [Record Task Delivery](../artifacts/task-body.md#record-task-delivery) with the task JSON, pull request records, complete issue-link snapshot, delivering pull request number, returned verified criterion ids and output body path.
   - Publish the returned body through [Save Tracker Issue](../artifacts/issue.md#save-tracker-issue) before closure.
   - Once the pull request has merged, record it with [Comment on Issue](../artifacts/issue.md#comment-on-issue): `Delivered by #950.`
   - [Issue Closure](../protocols/issue-closure.md) when it reports closable.
6. **Sync each epic.**
   Run [Record Epic Delivery](../artifacts/epic-issue-body.md#record-epic-delivery), linking every match from the match step, open or merged, with the task issues, the project checkout and the fetched epic bases its long-lived branch names are read at. Linking a pull request replaces the planning-record link on that task.
   - Handle the returned delivery findings:
     - **Normalized.**
       - The patch step publishes the corrected table.
     - **Retitle.**
       - Retitle the pull request to the title it names with [Publish Pull Request](../artifacts/pull-request.md#publish-pull-request).
     - **Conflict.**
       - Put it to the user.
     - **Unmatched.**
       - Match them as in the match step.
     - **In flight.**
       - Match them as in the match step.
     - **Draft.**
       - Open it as a draft review pull request.
       - Leave the epic open while its delivery is incomplete.
     - **Unmerged.**
       - The close step opens or merges that pull request.
     - **Target.**
       - Confirm the base it names against its work item's [Component](../artifacts/work-item.md#component): the confirmed base is the epic base of the long-lived branch that Component names, whether the finding names that base, another, or one of several.
         - A unit whose work items name several long-lived branches takes each task branch's base from the long-lived branch its last slug word names.
       - Retarget an open pull request to the confirmed base with [Publish Pull Request](../artifacts/pull-request.md#publish-pull-request).
       - Put a merged one to the user, since its merge cannot be moved.
     - **References.**
       - Bring the body up to the merges with [Review Pull Request](../protocols/review-pull-request.md), with the project checkout and the fetched epic bases.
     - **Changes.**
       - Restate the bullet naming the absent path with [Review Pull Request](../protocols/review-pull-request.md), with the project checkout and the fetched epic bases.
     - **No epic.**
       - Give it the epic it works on as the unnamed-deliveries step does, once the user confirms which.
     - **Uncited.**
       - Set the link with [Link Pull Request to Issue](../artifacts/pull-request.md#link-pull-request-to-issue).
       - Run [Fetch Pull Request Issue Links](../artifacts/pull-request.md#fetch-pull-request-issue-links) again.
     - **Note.**
       - Link the pull request as in the match step.
     - **Unplaced.**
       - Draft the missing task row against [Work Breakdown](../artifacts/epic-issue-body.md#work-breakdown).
       - Run [Check Plan Change Autonomy](../artifacts/plan-change.md#check-plan-change-autonomy) for the row, which is a task creation, with the allowance the caller supplied.
         - An automatic row is confirmed as drafted and recorded through [Record Plan Change](../artifacts/plan-change.md#record-plan-change).
         - A held row is settled as [Held Change](../artifacts/plan-change.md#held-change) states; an unanswered placement stays pending.
       - Apply the confirmed row through [Revise Epic Rows](../artifacts/epic-issue-body.md#revise-epic-rows).
       - Publish through [Save Tracker Issue](../artifacts/issue.md#save-tracker-issue).
       - Repeat Record Epic Delivery with the saved epic, refreshed task records and the same epic bases. An unanswered placement stays pending.
     - **Open questions.**
       - Return to the select step for this epic.
       - Resolve the questions there.
       - Fetch the saved body before repeating Record Epic Delivery with the same epic bases.
     - **Ready to verify.**
       - The verify step settles them.
     - **Unmet.**
       - The verify step settles the unticked criteria, planning a gap task for any that need further work.
     - **Ticked early.**
       - Untick them, or link the missing delivery.
     - **Disagreement.**
       - Continue recording links, verified criteria and Done despite the reported coverage disagreement.
     - **Unevaluable.**
       - Report each source and why to the user, with each check the run names not checked.
       - Leave an unmatched or in-flight pull request whose head is an epic base unmatched, since the run could not tell it from a task delivery.
       - Fetch each draft base, long-lived branch or review head named unread, and repeat Record Epic Delivery with the same epic bases.
       - The epic stays open until every epic base states the same readable declaration.
     - **Source.**
       - Report it with the results.
     - **Not checked.**
       - Report each check with the unevaluable sources that left it unread.
   - After applying the returned findings, repeat Record Epic Delivery with the revised epic body and refreshed delivery records, retaining the complete issue-link snapshot, the same epic bases and output body path. Recording the epic's delivery is finished when unmatched, in flight, uncited, note, unchanged, and unplaced are clear, apart from a pull request the user leaves unmatched.
7. **Verify.**
   Run [Verify Selected Criteria](../artifacts/acceptance-criteria.md#verify-selected-criteria) for the criteria reported ready to verify, supplying the current issue body, delivery findings, relevant delivery revisions, named instruments and the project checkout.
   - Retain the returned verified criterion ids and evidence for the tick step.
   - For an unresolved epic criterion requiring further work:
     - Follow [Plan Gap Task](../artifacts/epic-issue-body.md#plan-gap-task) with the current epic JSON and body, delivered task row, unmet criterion ids, delivery records, complete issue-link snapshot, project checkout, fetched epic bases and output body path.
     - For each criterion it returns as already holding, repeat [Verify Selected Criteria](../artifacts/acceptance-criteria.md#verify-selected-criteria) with that criterion id, the current epic body, delivery findings, delivery revisions, named instruments and the project checkout.
     - Pass the returned verified ids to [Tick Verified Criteria](../artifacts/acceptance-criteria.md#tick-verified-criteria) with the current epic JSON, pull request records, complete issue-link snapshot and output body path, and publish through [Save Tracker Issue](../artifacts/issue.md#save-tracker-issue).
     - Resume with its recorded disposition; a criterion that cannot be confirmed stays unticked.
8. **Tick.**
   Tick the confirmed criteria with [Tick Verified Criteria](../artifacts/acceptance-criteria.md#tick-verified-criteria).
9. **Patch.**
   Patch each changed body from its output body file with [Save Tracker Issue](../artifacts/issue.md#save-tracker-issue).
10. **Close.**
    - Run [Select Project Board](../artifacts/board.md#select-project-board) for the initiative theme when the caller supplied no board identity. Report an absent board; integration still follows its own evidence gates.
    - When [Record Epic Delivery](../artifacts/epic-issue-body.md#record-epic-delivery) reports an epic base unmerged and names no open pull request, open it as a draft review pull request and leave the epic open. Epic Integration establishes readiness from the completed delivery evidence.
    - For each open epic pull request:
      - Follow [Epic Integration](../protocols/epic-integration.md) with the epic identity and body, review identity, project checkout, current delivery records, complete issue-link snapshot, criterion verification evidence and selected board identity or its confirmed absence.
      - Report incomplete delivery or unmet merge requirements.
    - Fetch the pull requests again after merging.
    - Re-run [Record Epic Delivery](../artifacts/epic-issue-body.md#record-epic-delivery) with the refreshed records, the same project checkout and the same epic bases.
    - [Issue Closure](../protocols/issue-closure.md) each epic the re-run reports closable.
11. **Sync the initiative.**
    Run [Record Initiative Delivery](../artifacts/initiative-issue-body.md#record-initiative-delivery) with the epic JSON fetched after closing.
    - For returned criteria ready to verify:
      - Run [Verify Selected Criteria](../artifacts/acceptance-criteria.md#verify-selected-criteria) with their ids, current initiative body, delivery findings, delivery revisions, named instruments and the project checkout.
      - Pass returned verified ids to [Tick Verified Criteria](../artifacts/acceptance-criteria.md#tick-verified-criteria) with the initiative JSON, every linked epic record and output body file.
      - Report the remaining findings as pending.
    - [Save Tracker Issue](../artifacts/issue.md#save-tracker-issue) the initiative from its output body file when a tick changed it, so the board sync reads every criterion ticked.
    - [Issue Closure](../protocols/issue-closure.md) the initiative when it reports closable.
12. **Sync the board.**
    Run [Select Project Board](../artifacts/board.md#select-project-board) for the initiative's theme.
    - When the board is absent:
      - Read the originating proposal identified in the initiative's [References](../artifacts/initiative-issue-body.md#references) through [Read Tracker Issue](../artifacts/issue.md#read-tracker-issue); return unresolved provenance before board creation for a proposal-derived initiative.
      - Run [Copy Project Board](../artifacts/board.md#copy-project-board) with the owner, repository, theme title and originating proposal record when applicable.
    - Follow [Record Board Delivery](../artifacts/board-delivery.md#record-board-delivery) after the issue bodies and closures are saved.
13. **Explain each change entering review.**
    For each epic newly confirmed In Review by the board step:
    - Run [Understand Mode](understand-mode.md) with each epic review pull request, one run per base.
    - Complete each overview before continuing; an initiative has no overview of its own. An issue already In Review when the sync began keeps the overview it has: the pull request it explains is the one already reviewed. A reviewer meets the overview on the pull request it explains. The run that integrates an epic base owns that epic's overview; this step writes one only where the board step confirms an epic In Review that integration did not already explain.
14. **Report.**
    Return saved delivery results and unresolved findings to the caller, or present them to the user for a direct request.
    - Report queue decisions unevaluated by this run.
    - Run [Audit Closure Evidence](../artifacts/issue.md#audit-closure-evidence) for the repository holding the issues, naming the initiative, epics and tasks this run touched. Report each unsupported and unevaluable issue it returns, with its state reason and findings, and the not-planned closures apart. This run changes none of them.
    - Report per issue: tasks linked, criteria ticked, rows marked done, criteria left unticked and why, conflicts, test plan disagreements, what was closed, each board and assignee change, and each overview written. What the report names about criteria is [Coverage Reports](../artifacts/issue-body.md#coverage-reports).

# Board setup rehearsal

This is a local, read-only rehearsal. The supplied fixture is the evidence for board absence and proposal approval. No GitHub lookup, board copy, repository link, label creation, issue change, source edit, commit or publication has run.

## Resulting inputs

| Input | Value | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Owner | `m2ux` | Supplied fixture: user owner |
| Owner route | `users/m2ux` | Conventions: user-owned boards |
| Repository | `workflow-server` (`m2ux/workflow-server`) | Supplied fixture |
| Proposals board title | `Proposals` | Configuration → Proposals Board |
| Proposals copy-source title | `Proposals Template` | Configuration → Proposals Board; exact match, open board |
| Theme copy-source title | `Initiative Template` | Configuration → Theme Boards; exact match, open board |
| Originating proposal designator | `[P99]` | Supplied approved-proposal fixture; preserve both digits |
| Theme name | `Rehearsal` | Supplied fixture |
| Theme description | `Fixture Board Setup` | Supplied fixture |
| New theme board title | `[P99] Rehearsal: Fixture Board Setup` | Board → One Board Per Theme |

Template board numbers and the resulting board numbers are unknown. Example numbers in Conventions are not inputs. The fixture supplies no issue number, URL or saved proposal body for `[P99]`.

## Setup actions, pending live authority

Work on one board at a time, completing its repository link before continuing.

1. Prepare a checkout of `m2ux/workflow-server` for any eventual `gh` calls. Apply Conventions' session credential rule before the first call. Refresh the two absence findings and the approved originating proposal from live evidence when live access is authorized.
2. For the absent proposals board, follow Create Proposals Board:
   - Find the open board whose title exactly equals `Proposals Template` under `users/m2ux`; retain its returned number.
   - Copy that number with source owner `m2ux`, target owner `m2ux`, title `Proposals`.
   - Retain the copy response's `.number` and link that board to `workflow-server` under owner `m2ux`.
   - Return the board number only after linking succeeds.
3. For the absent Rehearsal board, follow Create Theme Board:
   - Carry the originating proposal record identifying `[P99]`; a missing designator blocks this operation. The rehearsal fixture supplies the designator, but its saved provenance still needs live readback.
   - Find the open board whose title exactly equals `Initiative Template` under `users/m2ux`; retain its returned number.
   - Copy that number with source owner `m2ux`, target owner `m2ux`, title `[P99] Rehearsal: Fixture Board Setup`.
   - Retain `.number`, link the board to `workflow-server`, and return its number after linking succeeds.
4. Read back each created board's identity, title, repository link and copied field configuration before reporting actual setup complete. Retain actual field and option IDs returned by the new boards; do not substitute template IDs or example IDs.
5. Before any initiative takes Rehearsal as its theme, satisfy Board → Copy Project Board's requirement for both the theme label and board. Repository Labels → Ensure Repository Labels needs the repository plus the label name, colour and description. `theme:rehearsal` is a candidate following the configuration examples, not a complete supplied definition. The colour and agreed description are absent; resolve the definition, list existing labels, then create it only if absent and authorized. Board copying itself does not publish an initiative or assign a theme label to issues.

The hypothetical copy inputs are:

```text
Find Board Template(owner=m2ux, template-title=Proposals Template)
Copy Board Template(owner=m2ux, template-number=<returned>, board-title=Proposals)
Link Board to Repository(owner=m2ux, board-number=<new>, repo=workflow-server)

Find Board Template(owner=m2ux, template-title=Initiative Template)
Copy Board Template(owner=m2ux, template-number=<returned>, board-title=[P99] Rehearsal: Fixture Board Setup)
Link Board to Repository(owner=m2ux, board-number=<new>, repo=workflow-server)
```

## Preserved fields and values

| Board | Required preserved configuration |
| --- | --- |
| Proposals | Priority options `High`, `Medium`, `Low`; view type board, grouped by `Status` |
| Rehearsal | Status options `Backlog`, `Ready`, `In Progress`, `In Review`, `Done` |

Copy the configured templates rather than assembling replacement fields. Preserve their other fields and views; their exact definitions are not supplied and have not been inspected. Board → Proposals defines the proposal lifecycle as `Suggested`, `Considering`, `Approved`, `Held`, `Declined`; inspect the proposals template's actual Status options and copied configuration against that lifecycle before claiming it is usable. This fixture does not authorize adding `[P99]` to a board or changing its status or assignee. If later authorized placement is required, the fixture's approved state must be considered explicitly; Propose's initial `Suggested` applies to a newly raised proposal.

## Remaining evidence and authority

- Actual authorized lookup results: open exact-title template identities and numbers, refreshed absence checks, unique intended matches, and the templates' full field/view definitions. Template availability is supplied; template identities are not.
